profile.address: 2551, North Arizona Avenue, Chandler, Maricopa County, Arizona, 85225
profile.reading:
The Maricopa County, Arizona address associated with this facility, near 2551 North Arizona Avenue in Chandler, is tied to StrongMind, a K-12 digital education company rather than a data center operator in the commercial sense. StrongMind traces its roots to 2000, when it was founded as the Institute for Educational Development, and took its current name in a 2015 rebrand. The company, led by founder and chief executive Damian Creamer, builds curriculum and learning platforms for homeschool families and for schools that want to offer digital and online courses, and in recent years it has added StrongMind Central, a learning management platform, and StrongMind Intelligence, an artificial intelligence layer built into its coursework. In February 2026 the company was named to a Top 25 Global Impact Certified EdTech Company list in the High Impact category, a sign that its business is curriculum and learning outcomes rather than hosting infrastructure for other companies.

Chandler sits in the East Valley of the Phoenix metropolitan area, a corridor that has attracted a mix of chip manufacturing, cloud campuses, and technology back offices over the past two decades because of relatively affordable land, a large workforce, and aggressive local incentives. A company like StrongMind, which serves students and school districts across the country through web based platforms, needs meaningful server and network capacity to run those platforms reliably, and a Chandler office building is a plausible place to house that equipment alongside curriculum development, customer support, and administrative staff.

Nothing on StrongMind's public site describes this address as a data center, states a square footage for technical space, or discloses a power capacity in megawatts, and no separate colocation or wholesale hosting business is marketed under the StrongMind name. That absence is itself informative. It points to this location functioning as corporate infrastructure serving StrongMind's own operations rather than as a facility built or marketed to host equipment for outside customers. Companies that sell colocation space typically publish exactly the kind of specification sheet that StrongMind does not, because prospective tenants need to compare power, cooling, and connectivity before signing a contract. StrongMind's silence on those points is consistent with a private, single tenant facility rather than a gap in an otherwise public record.

reading.body:
This entry represents internal server or office infrastructure for an edtech company, not a dedicated data center facility, and contributes zero megawatts to AI infrastructure capacity.

StrongMind is a K-12 digital learning provider. Its Maricopa County address appears in data center registries but lacks published specifications on power capacity, square footage, or colocation services. The company's own site identifies it as a curriculum and homeschool platform operator, not a marketed cloud or data center provider.

The distinction matters because infrastructure inventories can conflate internal IT operations with the specialized facilities that power AI workloads. A company that runs servers to deliver its own service occupies a different category than a colocation provider or hyperscaler whose power consumption directly scales with compute demand. This entry, verified complete as of September 2026, contributes no measurable electricity consumption to the grid load that constrains AI scaling.

Maricopa County hosts genuine AI infrastructure facilities elsewhere. This row shows how public registries can obscure signal with categorical noise if operator type is not verified.
